title: Analogies between species of large genera and varieties support descent

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Analogies between species of large genera and varieties support descent

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The analogies between species of large genera and varieties (more varieties, small and unequal differences, restricted ranges) are understandable if species once existed as varieties, and inexplicable if each species was independently created.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And we can clearly understand these analogies, if species have once existed as varieties, and have thus originated: whereas, these analogies are utterly inexplicable if each species has been independently created.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter II, “Variation under Nature”; section “Summary”. Scope: species and varieties of plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch02-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The analogies are measurable and descent makes quantitative clustering predictions, but 'utterly inexplicable' is not a well-specified rival. Existing data strongly assess comparative fit without logically excluding every creation model.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the joint observed patterns of genus size, infraspecific variation, relatedness and range size under explicit branching-descent models versus independent-origin models. Strong likelihood or predictive advantage for descent supports the inference.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Independent creation has no agreed probabilistic model.

The listed analogies are not independent of taxonomy.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.67
analysis feasibility: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.57
discriminating power: 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The component patterns can be measured with trees, floras, and ranges, so the factual bundle is partly open to analysis. The contrast with independent creation is poorly discriminating because that rival does not forbid a specific outcome. A missing bundle would hurt the argument, while a present bundle would still be compatible with more than one historical story.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test the bundle of variety-like statistics for species in large genera (more infraspecific forms, small unequal gaps, restricted ranges of close allies) and ask whether that bundle is predicted by descent of species from varieties. Failure of the bundle would undermine the explanatory claim; success would favour descent only relative to a creation hypothesis that forbids variety-like structure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The analogies are the same facts used in the neighbouring variety-and-genus claims, and a joint test double-counts them.

Descent predicts the bundle only after extra assumptions about rates and extinction.

Independent creation can be adjusted to produce any observed pattern, so confirmation is weak.
